newsitem.title: THAILAND: Flower power blossoms in Thai election.
newsitem.headline: Flower power blossoms in Thai election.

text.p: Rival parties in Thailand's upcoming election are all sporting garlands of marigolds -- delighting flower sellers but upsetting worshippers who cannot afford the blooming prices.

Marigolds or "Daoruang" in Thai have became the most popular campaign flower among the thousands of candidates standing for the polls on November 17 because it means "bright star" and people believe its auspicious name will bring them luck.

"These flowers turned my white shirt yellow one day when I had to speak in the rain but I am ready to accept them with great pleasure because they carry an auspicious name," Trairong Suwankiri, a Democrat candidate, told a Bangkok rally recently.

But with strong demand from the more than 2,000 parliamentary candidates those benefiting most appear to be the nation's many flower vendors. Marigold prices have rocketed from 25 baht ($1) per 100 flowers to up to 60 baht.
But the strong demand has upset worshippers wanting to make flower offerings in temples, Sunun Wilavan, a vendor at a popular Hindu shrine, told Reuters.
The Thai Farmer Bank Research Co Ltd said a marigold garland now cost around 100 baht ($4).
There are no statistics, but a campaign organiser at a political party estimated that at least 200 garlands were used at every major election rally.
"So I estimate that at each party would spend more than two million baht for marigold flowers during the four-week campaign," said the organiser, who declined to be identified.
